$status: Vertical landmarks set from standard adult-female anthropometry as fractions of stature (2026-08-10) — they are no longer guesses and should not be nudged by eye. Circumferences are a standard size for this height. $fromThupten still marks anything he has confirmed for Ü-Tsang specifically.
$proportions: Fractions of stature used, from standard anthropometric tables: chin 0.870, shoulder (acromion) 0.818, bust 0.720, underbust 0.700, waist 0.620, hip 0.520, knee 0.285, ankle 0.039. Head height is stature/7.7 — chin to crown — which is the realistic adult figure, not the 8-head heroic one.
$unit: cm, measured from the floor with the figure standing
$worldScale: cm per solver world unit. The solver's approved feel is tuned at particle spacing 1.0, so cloth resolution is worldScale cm between particles. 2.5 cm is a normal garment-sim resolution.

$notes.height: Total including head, floor to crown.
$notes.floorToChin: Chin height, 0.870 of stature. The neck must STOP here — it ran past the chin and read as a giraffe.
$notes.floorToNeckBase: Top ring of the torso lathe: where the neck emerges from the trapezius. NOT the anthropometric cervicale (0.828), which sits about level with the shoulder point — using that flattened her shoulders into a square slab. The gap between this and floorToShoulder over the half-width between them IS the shoulder slope, and it should come out around 21 degrees, the same slope the garment is drafted to.
$notes.headWidth: Head breadth in front view. The dress form has no head for the solver; this is for drawing one at the right size.
$notes.floorToWaist: Where the belt sits. The single most important number on this list: it sets the pinned/free boundary, so it decides how much of the garment simulates at all.
$notes.floorToHip: Fullest part of the seat. Sets where the skirt stops touching and starts hanging.
$notes.shoulderWidth: Across the back, point to point. Sets strap placement on a sleeveless chupa.
$notes.depthRatio: Cross-sections are ellipses, not circles: depth divided by width at each level. 1.0 would be a cylinder-round body. These four control how the silhouette reads in three-quarter view and are pure guesswork on my part.
$notes.armSeparation: Gap from the body centreline to each arm's axis. Arms are capsules; they only matter where the honju sleeve hangs against them. Must leave the arm inboard of the shoulder point — at shoulderWidth 37 the shoulder is 18.5 out, so an arm of ~4.3 radius wants an axis around 14. At 17 the sleeve stood proud of the shoulder and the outfit read wrong.
